Q: How is the MIME type of an uploaded file determined by the browser? A:

I spent some time reading RFCs, MSDN and MDN. Here is what I could understand.

When a browser encounters a file for upload, it looks at the first buffer of data it receives and then runs a test on it. These tests try to determine if the file is a known MIME type or not, and if known MIME type it will simply further test it for which known MIME type and take action accordingly.

I think Internet Explorer tries to do this first rather than just determining the file type from extension. This page explains this for Internet Explorer: MIME Type Detection in Windows Internet Explorer.

For firefox, I could understand that it tries to read file information from filesystem or directory entry and then determines the file type. Here is a link for Firefox https://developer.mozilla.org/en/XPCOM_Interface_Reference/nsIFile. I would still like to have more authoritative information on this.
